comparison: Strong agreement on activity-dependent mechanism claims (C115, C125-C132). Both evaluations find the Hebbian/activity-dependent interpretation well-supported. OpenEval notes the model is inferential rather than directly tested, while peer reviewers explicitly endorse it as consistent with data and prior literature on retinal waves.

Strong agreement on LIN connectivity findings (C74-C86). Both evaluations support the differential behavior of LIN dendrites and mixed connectivity patterns. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of optical and EM evidence, while peer reviewers highlight this as a strength showing interesting differences between TC and LIN neurons.

Strong agreement on ultrastructural characterization (C25-C40). Both evaluations affirm the quality of combined light and EM data showing normal glomerular structure and absence of anatomical barriers. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the high-resolution methods as a major strength.

Strong agreement on complete synaptic segregation (C4, C45, C50-C59, C64). Both evaluations find this central finding compelling and well-supported by EM reconstruction data. OpenEval notes sample from single animal; peer reviewers acknowledge limited sample size but emphasize the achievement and impact of demonstrating complete segregation.

Strong agreement on main conclusion about system capacity for segregation (C5, C88, C91, C101-C102, C112-C113). Both evaluations support the interpretation that the data demonstrate the mouse dLGN's capacity for complete input segregation despite its small size.

Strong agreement on adaptive organization interpretation (C101-C103). Both evaluations support the claim that the system has capacity for segregation. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly endorses this as impactful, directly addressing the capacity question.

Agreement on statistical validation (C61-C63). OpenEval finds Monte Carlo analysis appropriately demonstrates segregation exceeds chance. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this through their endorsement of the complete segregation finding, though they don't separately discuss the statistical approach.

Agreement on technical methods (C46-C49). OpenEval finds technical choices appropriately justified. Peer Reviewer 1 identifies CLEM approach as a strength for testing circuit-level hypotheses, and reviewers accept the methodological rigor despite limited sample size.

Overlap on statistical validation (C61-C62) within broader methodological assessment. OpenEval specifically evaluates Monte Carlo analysis; peer reviewers accept the statistical validation implicitly as part of the compelling evidence package.

Agreement on TC dendritic morphology (C66-C68, C134, C137-C138). OpenEval finds dendritic asymmetry well-supported by EM data. Peer reviewers don't raise concerns and implicitly accept these morphological findings as part of the valuable connectivity descriptions.

Divergent evaluation of exclusion zone mechanism (C133-C138, C142). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the dendritic remodeling mechanism is speculative and cited evidence is from different contexts. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting it as reasonable inference without challenging the speculation.

Related to dendritic morphology interpretation (C134, C137-C138). OpenEval finds the remodeling mechanism speculative; peer reviewers accept morphological descriptions without qualification, suggesting implicit support for the interpretation.

Agreement on retinal wave blocking evidence (C3, C23, C110-C111). Both evaluations accept cited prior work (Rebsam et al.) as established evidence. OpenEval notes current manuscript doesn't perform these experiments; peer reviewers incorporate this as part of the activity-dependent mechanism support.

Agreement on optical imaging of islands (C1, C20-C22, C24). Both evaluations support these descriptive findings. OpenEval emphasizes consistency across 12 mice and agreement with literature; peer reviewers affirm quality of confocal imaging without raising concerns.

Agreement on LIN background/organization (C70-C73). OpenEval finds these claims accurately represent prior work with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this background as part of their endorsement of the LIN connectivity findings.

Divergent evaluation of speculative claims (C103, C106, C122). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting these are speculative hypotheses beyond what data support. Peer Reviewer 2 appears to accept the adaptive balance interpretation (C103) as part of the capacity argument, suggesting implicit support.

OpenEval evaluates cortical feedback specificity (C69) as SUPPORTED, demonstrating segregation is specific to retinogeniculate connectivity. No corresponding separate evaluation in peer reviews, though this may be implicitly accepted as part of the overall connectivity characterization.

OpenEval evaluates background claims on dLGN development (C6-C19) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers don't separately evaluate background/context claims, focusing instead on novel findings and interpretations.

OpenEval evaluates prior work context (C41-C44, C89-C100) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and species comparisons. Peer reviewers don't separately assess literature review claims, though they reference this context in discussing the study's significance.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic literature claims (C104-C109, C116-C121, C139-C141) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers don't separately evaluate these background mechanism claims from the literature.

OpenEval evaluates inference about normal development (C123-C124) as SUPPORTED but not directly demonstrated. Peer reviewers don't separately address these inferential claims about typical developmental processes.
